fields.description_1:
Devrijesmid sells craftsmanship through work that is made for a specific place or purpose. A potential client may arrive with an idea for custom metalwork but not know the technical name, production method or exact specification. The website therefore had to show the range of work without turning every project into a product that can simply be copied.

Project examples needed to demonstrate style and capability while service information explained how a new enquiry can begin. The copy also had to respect the difference between inspiration and a confirmed technical solution. On mobile, images could not push the practical route to contact out of view. The portfolio challenge was to present specialist metalwork clearly, using real project proof without promising identical results for future commissions.
fields.description_2:
I built Devrijesmid around the work itself, using project examples as the first proof of what the craft can involve. Supporting text then explains the relevant metalwork and the route from an initial idea to a conversation, without pretending that a custom commission can be selected like a standard catalogue item.

Enquiry actions sit close to the examples and service context so visitors can describe what they need after seeing comparable work. I kept the wording simple and avoided exaggerated claims about craftsmanship that the portfolio images should prove for themselves. On smaller screens, imagery, explanation and contact follow a clear order. The case now shows how WordPress supports a visual custom-work portfolio while keeping the next practical step easy to understand.

fields.description_1:
Palmeroshop offers recovery products that can look similar, especially to shoppers who are new to massage guns or related wellness equipment. Product pages therefore need to explain practical differences without turning general product information into medical advice. A customer should be able to compare the offer, understand the controls or included features and decide whether to continue to the cart.

The webshop also had to stay easy to use on mobile, where long feature lists can hide price and purchase actions. Claims about pain relief, recovery speed or health outcomes needed particular care because those results depend on the person and use. The portfolio problem was to create a clear product-shopping route while keeping the language useful, commercial and appropriately cautious about health-related benefits.
fields.description_2:
I organised Palmeroshop so shoppers can move from the recovery category to individual products and compare the details that belong to the purchase decision. Product information, pricing and cart actions remain connected, while supporting explanations help customers understand the equipment without presenting it as a guaranteed medical solution.

I kept health-related wording measured and avoided promises about pain, rehabilitation or recovery time that require clinical evidence. On mobile, product images, key details, price and add-to-cart actions follow a predictable sequence instead of competing for attention. The WooCommerce structure keeps the buying path familiar while allowing each item to explain its own features. The portfolio case now reflects a specialist recovery-products shop rather than a generic ecommerce layout with unsupported wellness claims.

fields.description_1:
Woningontruimingvergelijken serves people who may be arranging a clearance during a move, estate situation or property handover. They often need to understand what a clearance can include before comparing providers, and local availability may matter. A simple directory would not explain the job well enough to support a useful quote request.

The platform therefore needed to connect guidance with provider comparison and a form that captures the information companies need. It also had to avoid suggesting that every provider offers the same service, price or timing. On mobile, guidance and the request flow needed to remain readable without a long detour. The portfolio challenge was to help households move from an uncertain clearance need to comparable enquiries while keeping claims about providers and outcomes evidence-based.
fields.description_2:
I structured Woningontruimingvergelijken around the questions that come before a quote request. Practical information helps visitors define the clearance need first, after which the platform can guide them toward provider comparison and a request containing the details that matter. This makes the form part of the decision process instead of an isolated lead box.

Local or service information stays close to the comparison it supports, while wording avoids implying identical prices, availability or service quality across providers. On smaller screens, guidance, form fields and next steps follow a compact order. The portfolio case now explains the actual comparison journey: understand the task, provide relevant information and request suitable offers, without claiming savings or provider performance that have not been independently measured.

fields.description_1:
Solardaktechnique combines roofing work with solar-related services, which creates a decision that is more technical than choosing one product. A property owner may be considering roof condition, solar installation or both, and the right sequence depends on the building. Presenting these topics separately without context could leave visitors unsure which issue should be discussed first.

The website therefore needed to connect roof and solar routes while keeping property-specific advice central. Examples could show the type of work, but they could not guarantee energy yield, system size or identical installation conditions. On mobile, service choices and quotation access needed a simple hierarchy. The portfolio problem was to make two related technical disciplines understandable together without turning site copy into a promise about savings, performance or suitability.
fields.description_2:
I organised Solardaktechnique so visitors can start with the roof, the solar question or the combination that affects both. Separate service sections explain the relevant work, while project context shows how roofing and solar can relate without assuming that every property needs the same approach. The structure leaves room for technical assessment before a solution is presented as final.

Quotation and advice actions appear after the key context, giving property owners a clear point to share details about the building. I kept energy claims conservative and avoided promises about yield, payback or savings without project-specific evidence. On smaller screens, service cards, examples and calls to action keep the same order. The portfolio case now reflects a combined roof-and-solar decision journey rather than generic installation marketing.

fields.description_1:
Neturalhome speaks to homeowners who want a sustainable, comfortable property but may not know which improvement should come first. Energy-related options can affect each other, and general sustainability language cannot help someone choose a relevant service. The website needed to turn a broad ambition into understandable routes without implying that one solution fits every home.

Practical benefits had to be explained alongside limitations and the need for property-specific advice. Claims about lower bills, comfort or environmental impact also needed restraint because real results depend on the building, behaviour and chosen measures. On mobile, homeowners should still be able to compare the main options and reach advice quickly. The portfolio challenge was to make sustainable home improvement approachable without reducing it to generic green promises.
fields.description_2:
I structured Neturalhome around the home improvements people can actually explore rather than around broad sustainability statements. Each option has its own explanation, helping a homeowner understand what the measure is for before moving into deeper detail or asking for advice. Supporting information stays close to the choice it clarifies.

I kept expected benefits descriptive rather than guaranteed, because energy use, comfort and financial impact vary by property and household. Advice actions appear after enough context for a useful conversation, and the mobile layout keeps service cards and next steps easy to scan. The portfolio case now shows how WordPress can turn a broad sustainable-home proposition into clear decision routes while avoiding claims that every measure will produce the same savings, performance or environmental result.
